text: Six weeks of TMS can lift a depression. Then the daily visits end, and for many people, it quietly comes back. Not all at once. In ordinary weeks, when nobody is there to notice.
We believe staying well should feel like being gently noticed. Not monitored, scored, or nagged. That's Tiiramisu.

Each day, there's a thirty-second voice check-in. On her phone, it hears how Aino sounds, her pace, her pauses, her energy, compared only with her own usual, alongside her sleep and the rhythm of her days. Weeks later, it notices something she hasn't said. Her days and nights are blending, and her voice is quieter.

It offers a step sized for today, smaller on harder days. She guesses how much it'll help. Afterwards, she notices it helped more than she expected. Every small step makes the room a little warmer. And whether she checks in every day, or comes back after a while, the room is never cold. It only gets warmer. We reward. We encourage. We nurture. No streaks, no scores, nothing to lose.
Over time, it learns what actually helps her, and lets the people who have her back cheer her on, but only if she chooses.
The loop works on its own. When it matters, her clinic can see who has drifted, with a short summary, and reach out with one tap.
Her voice is never stored. Her data stays in the EU, and every build proves exactly where it goes.
Because staying well shouldn't depend on being in the clinic.
